recentItems.title: A rural island in Turkey is home to geese, wild rabbits and one man
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
TURKEY ISLAND GEESE 

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

LENGTH: 3:13

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Ciplak Island, Balikesir province, Turkey - 21 August 2026
1. Wide then zoom in of boat approaching Ciplak Island and geese paddling toward boat
2. Various of geese approaching boat
3. Tugrul Ugur, a boat captain, feeding geese 
4. Mid of geese eating
5. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Tugrul Ugur, boat captain:  ++GEESE HONKING AT END OF BITE++
"These are wild geese, not domesticated ones. I’ve been visiting regularly for two, three years. There is life here, and we have an acquaintance in the area, so we go back and forth thanks to that connection. They (the geese) have grown accustomed to me because I feed them constantly."

6. Various of Ugur feeding the geese bread
7. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Tugrul Ugur, boat captain: ++GEESE HONKING++
"They (geese) come flying over when they see me. The animals have gotten used to me. My love for animals plays a big part in this, of course. It’s not just the geese. For instance, there are thousands of rabbits on our island, wild ones, too, and they act the same way."

8. Geese 
9. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Tugrul Ugur, boat captain: 
"Its (island) name is Ciplak Ada because it is pristine. Or rather, because there are no trees or anything of that sort. There is a settlement of only four or five homes. Apart from that, we have some very fine freshwater wells on our island."

10. Various of geese honking on land 
11. Various of wild rabbits on island
12. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Hizir Ates, island resident: 
"I love this life. I love solitude. Not everyone could do this, live here. Some people don’t want to give up city life. It’s all over. It’s all finished (meaning everything in life has been ruined)."

13. Ates in front of his home, looking into a plastic drum
14. Cutaway of socks hanging up to dry 
15. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Hizir Ates, island resident: 
"I have sheep. I used to milk the sheep and (obtain) about 150-160 kg (330-350 pounds of milk). But now I raise lambs, I do it all myself."

16. Wide of island, wild rabbit running in the distance 
STORYLINE:
A local population of wild geese on an Aegean island off the coast of western Turkey suddenly start honking enthusiastically as a boat approaches the beach. 

They waddle toward shore and glide into the water in formation, furiously paddling toward the vessel. 

They know who’s coming. It’s Tugrul Ugur, a full-time 40-year-old animal lover and part-time boat captain. 

He spends his summers ferrying tourists to local attractions, including Ciplak Island, a nearly-deserted piece of land near Ayvalik, nestled in between Turkey and the neighboring Greek island of Lesvos. 

He always packs plenty of bread for the resident geese who “come flying” when they see him. 

It appears the flock is able to identify him, and the drone of his boat engine. 

The animated reunion between man and animal has become an endearing routine. 

Ashore, the island’s wild rabbits are much shyer, their welcome more subdued than that of the birds.

They mostly keep their distance, often darting away to hide in the sparse vegetation. 

But Ugur makes sure to bring food for them too. 

"The animals have gotten used to me. My love for animals plays a big part in this," he says. 

The animals aren't the only residents of Ciplak Island, whose name translates to ‘bare’ or ‘naked’ in Turkish. 

Hizir Ates is the only full-time resident and has lived there alone for more than 40 years. 




AP Video by Mehmet Guzel
Production by Ayse Wieting

recentItems.title: Pop princess talks about life, love and chocolate
recentItems.description:
(19 Jan 2002) 

STORYLINE:

14 mins approx
1. Sit down interview with Britney Spears. Talks on: 'Crossroads' and how close her character Lucy is to herself, why she chose to go into films, on critics opinions of the film, love scenes in the film and awkwardness, single 'Overprotected' and its relevance to her life, keeping control over her career, HBO special and its theatrical nature, 'Not A Girl, Not Yet a Woman' single and her view on the meaning, biggest misconception in the press (about being a huge star), attacks in the press, new album and releasing 'Boys' as a single, acting in 'Austin Powers', press making up stories, being thought of as a diva, working with The Neptunes, her style, on marriage rumours, being a role model and labelled as an inspiration, what keeps her working, loving her life, having no regrets, attending premieres of 'Crossroads', visiting different countries promoting the films. Including soundbites:
"I like to talk about my work and the stuff that I do but when they start getting too personal then I am like OK, that's for me and not you. "
"I'm really happy and hopefully he is really happy but that is something that we will definitely do in the future but not right now, we are both really busy doing what we do and having fun with what we do. That is something, that if it did happen it would be in the future."
"That's why I am where I am today, because I do have control and you control what you do, you have to otherwise you get sucked in by people that are not necessary and so you have to continue to stay in control."
"It's just more me and it feels good. I'm singing the kind of songs that I like and, you know, I think it's more hip hop and R 'n' B orientated and, you know, it just feels good."
"I think I can more relate to that song - probably Britney three years ago when I was just leaving my home and my mom was kind of like 'Oh, my baby's leaving me now' you know? I think all teenagers when they're about to go off to college, they kind of get a sense of that feeling of being overprotected because, you know, it was just a matter of my mom respecting the fact that I'm becoming a woman and my dad just trusting me you know? But my protection now is the kind of protection that's necessary." 
"They are the coolest guys in the whole world - I absolutely love them. Like when they're in the studio, I have people and producers who take what they do really really seriously, you go in with them and they're just there to have a good time and just to do what they love and that was how it felt when I was there in the studio with them. They were the nicest guys and hopefully in the future I'll work with them again. That would be very cool."
"I just see myself as just like everyone else. If I say I was a role-model then it's kind of like putting a label on yourself. I just try to be myself and have a good time with what I do and hopefully people will see that and be inspired by me. I do like being labelled as an inspiration you know,  I would love to be an inspiration for people - not a role model you know?"  
"I think that's so sad that people say that, because, you know, we get inspired just like everybody else and that's the funnest part about what I do, is that I can be inspired to make up new clothes, and to have new designs, that's a part of what I do and that's why we are looked up to because  people follow that. So why do they have misconceptions that people tell us you know? I think it's kind of funny."
"No I think that if I've done something that has been a mistake I've learnt from it and it's made me a stronger person - so I don't have any regrets, no."

recentItems.description:
(31 Mar 1994) 

STORYLINE:
EF 605D - ITALY: HERITAGE 
t/c 16:43-21:40
SYNOPSIS: 
Venice has been sinking ever since the city was begun, over one thousand years ago.  Today, she is beset by flood tides, industrial pollution, and contaminated air and water.  The effort to save Venice - to rehabilitate her buildings and art treasures - is an on-going one, and involves international efforts from governments, scientific organisations, philanthropic groups, and art historical societies.  Twentieth-century living is taking its toll on this ancient and unique city. 
Scientific research is discovering ways to preserve the beauty that is Venice.  UNESCO has increased its office on the Grand Canal - using Venice as its main centre for marine and atmospheric research.  An increase in funds from the Italian government means there is more money and attention to the problems of Venice.  Private industry, too, has participated in the restoration process, refurbishing palazzos on the canals.  Preserving the facade of Venice is a lengthy and expensive process ... one without an end in sight. 
SHOWS: Floods ("aqua alta") of Nov 4/5, 1966; St Mark's Square with souvenir stands (looking towards church); St Mark's Square (looking away from church) with pigeons, drainage holes in paving blocks; graphic showing drainage under St Mark's square; Doge's Palace; gondolas in Grand Canal; gondolas travel along smaller canals: under bridge, past laundry hanging; slime and decay along small canals; UNESCO exterior along Grand Canal; UNESCO office director, Vladimir Kuznetzov walks in garden behind UNESCO palazzo; Kuznetzov speaks in English; facade of San Zulian (San Guiliemo) church, close up of restoration work sign, workers with chemical sprays and chisels restore facade; John Millerchip of private British charitable organization Venice in Peril speaks in English; restorers work on facade as Millerchip looks on; exterior of building housing old Jewish synagogue; panoramic interior views of restored synagogue Scuola Canton; vaporetto stop along Grand Canal; ancient key unlocks gate of ancient Jewish cemetery on Venice Lido (beach); interior walking shots inside cemetery showing tombstones, graves in need of repair; vaporetto (type of water-bus) full of tourists; Venice University Professor Paolo Lanapoppi speaks in English; Palazzo Grassi (restored palace now a museum) exterior; interior Palazzo Grassi shots showing tourists, ticket booth , atrium; pan of ancient restored ceiling to modern museum area; people looking at artwork; museum rooms; restored central staircase in Palazzo Grassi; shots of Grand Canal in twilight; gondolas with serenades in twilight; Chiesa della Salute (white church) along Grand Canal in twilight.

recentItems.title: Sit down interviews with cast from Inception
recentItems.description:
(21 Jul 2010) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, 8 July 2010
Approx 25 mins
Tape 1
1. Sit down interview with Joseph Gordon-Levitt including the following sound bites:
''No, I mean everything you're saying it true. So.''
"Coming off the success of 'The Dark Knight' he got to do whatever he wanted to do and it's a beautiful thing to see because he's the genuine article. He's not coming from a standpoint of business or market research, 'Inception' is the product of the work he's been doing for 10 years and to see that kind of story get told on such a grand scale, that is rare."
2. Sit down interview with Ellen Page including the following sound bites: 
''Dick Cheney. Dick Cheney maybe, Sarah Palin. Maybe a little seed of compassion or some holistic intellegence and maybe a little expansion of minds and maybe get rid of some of that fear that seems to be creating a lot of ignorance and thus passing on that fear to a lot of people and causing a lot of problems. Is that too much? Did I just go to far?"
''OK.''
"It has a complexity to it and literally multi-dimensional and being able to work with Chris every day and talk to Chris about certain existentialist questions that come up while being involved with this film is really quite a treat and I think makes the process even that much more fantastic because you're working with a director who's absurdly talented and who has just written this incredibly original screenplay."
FURTHER RESTICTIONS: NONE
TAPE FORMAT: DIGI BETACAM
USED FOR STORIES: 635060
TAPE 2
3. Sit down interview with Christopher Nolan including the following sound bites:
"I like to work one on one as much as possible so they can't gang up on me but then once you've had enough one on one conversations then you know where they stand on the character then you start to bring them together and look at a couple at a time. But I never brought the whole group together because I thought really we wanted to do that on film and it worked very well. I thought they all came together as a group dynamic on set very nicely, very much the way the characters have to in the story."
FURTHER RESTRICTIONS: NONE
TAPE FORMAT: DIGI BETACAM
USED FOR STORIES:
TAPE 3
4. Sid down interview with Leonardo DiCaprio including the following sound bites:
"We talked about his film and the rules of Chris Nolan's dream world at great length, we really spent months trying to take apart this puzzle and put it back together again. He'd been brewing over these concepts for something like 8 or 10 years and this was the culmination of all that thought. So for me I try to take a traditional approach, initially, as far as how I was going to research this character but I realized the only way to do it was to delve into this guy's mind and with him try and create an interesting compelling narrative for my character's journey."
"I was blown away, I was truly on the edge of my seat throughout the entire process of not only making the movie but watching it. We were immersed in a lot of these environments, Chris uses very little green screen, so if there's a tilting set or if you're in the middle of an avalanche he puts you there and you have to react accordingly. But to be able to see the way he intercut all these different visuals and all these different states of the human subconscious and places in the world and how all the characters connect is pretty astounding, he is masterful with that."
FURTHER RESTRICTIONS: NONE
TAPE FORMAT: DIGI BETACAM

recentItems.title: China MOFA briefing highlights
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

MOFA Highlights                                      
Spokesperson: Lin Jian
Date: 25 Aug 2026
Duration:  02 min 36 sec


ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Beijing, China -  25 August 2026

1. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday announced a package of economic sanctions against Iran and threatened to impose secondary sanctions on countries that do not join the US actions. What is China's comment?

We have made clear on many occasions that China firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that lack a basis in international law and have not been authorized by the United Nations Security Council. Economic warfare and maximum pressure cannot help resolve issues, which will only further exacerbate tensions, cause risks to spill over, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and harm the legitimate rights and interests of other countries. The most urgent task is to de-escalate the situation and return to the path of dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible. China will take all necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its rights and interests.

2.To follow up on the US sanctions on Iran, we have seen some new sanctions targeting individuals, entities and vessels, including some Chinese companies. What is the spokesperson's comment? In China's engagement with Iran, is China willing to change some of its practices to comply with US requirements? What measures is China considering taking?

China-Iran cooperation has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined. China is closely monitoring relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its own rights and interests.

3.At the second World Humanoid Robot Games, Chinese-made robots have broken several world records, including those in the human 100-meter sprint and men's high jump, sparking heated discussion around the world. But some commentators say the prospects for industrial application and commercialization of the sector remain unclear, while measures by some countries to guard against and restrict China's high-tech industries could also create obstacles to China's commitment to sharing opportunities with the world. What is the spokesperson's comment?

The underlying logic behind China’s development of new-quality productive forces and promotion of sci-tech innovation is openness, cooperation, mutual benefit, and win-win outcomes, not the imposition of artificial restrictions, isolation, or monopolization. We are ready to work with countries around the world to continue dialogue and cooperation in cutting-edge areas such as artificial intelligence and embodied intelligence, so that “Created in China” and “Made in China” can truly become drivers of shared development. We will tap into the potential for cooperation through technological exchange, joint standard-setting and market sharing, and ensure that the benefits of innovation are shared more widely by all of humanity.

4.The Trump administration is reportedly considering a $100,000 fee for employers hiring foreign workers. Given that 12% of H-1B visa applicants are from China, what is China's comment?

I have no comment on the US visa policy. 
STORYLINE:

recentItems.title: Indonesians brave choking smoke to pray for rain as country battles wildfires
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Palembang, South Sumatra, Indonesia -  25 August 2026
1. Various of firefighters battling flames spreading near a residential area
2. Various of worshippers performing prayers
3. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Tony Kurniawan, worshipper and local resident:
++AUDIO QUALITY AS INCOMING++
“We are praying together and also asking for the support of all people in South Sumatra, so that rain will fall soon, the forest and land fires will end, and the air can return to normal.”
4. Various of prayers
5. Various of firefighters battling flames spreading near a residential area
STORYLINE:
Authorities in Indonesia’s South Sumatra, the province with the highest number of wildfire hot spots, turned to spiritual measures on Tuesday as huge blazes in central and western regions scorched wide areas of forests and peatland, creating a choking haze that blanketed some cities in the world’s most populous Muslim-majority country.

The prayer gathering initiative comes as the province faces prolonged dry weather that has heightened the risk of forest and peatland fires.

The latest satellite data from the Environment Ministry showed South Sumatra recorded the highest number of hot spots nationwide with 1,429, followed by West Kalimantan with 1,226 and Central Kalimantan with 811. 

Forestry Ministry data indicated that nearly 940 square kilometers (363 square miles) were burned in July alone, including over 20 square kilometers (8 square miles) in South Sumatra province.

About 3,000 residents gathered in Palembang, the capital of South Sumatra province, to perform a special Islamic prayer for rain, known as “salat istisqa.” 

They prayed shoulder to shoulder in the courtyard of the governor’s office as thick smoke shrouded roads, buildings and public facilities, reducing visibility and forcing motorists to drive with their headlights on during the day.

South Sumatra Gov. Herman Deru said that everyone has done everything they can and worked closely with all relevant parties before the prayer. 

He added that as people of faith, they are praying to God to send rain so that life can return to normal.

He also said the public prayer would complement ongoing firefighting and drought-mitigation measures and serve as a moment for residents to unite in confronting the environmental challenges facing the province.

Emergency services have been battling fires driven by an intensifying El Nino pattern and a prolonged dry season, generating dense smoke that crossed into Malaysia and Brunei, according to the National Disaster Management Agency.

Indonesia is actively intensifying weather-modification operations to help firefighters combat wildfires by inducing rainfall through the dispersal of salt particles into suitable clouds, with 30 aircraft for cloud-seeding and water-bombing operations over Kalimantan, and another 22 helicopters covering Sumatra.

Indonesian police have arrested 72 people suspected of starting some of the forest and peatland fires, while four companies are under investigation for allegedly using fire to clear land at low cost.

Plantation owners and traditional farmers often start fires to clear land for farming, triggering hazardous haze that reduces visibility, disrupts land and air transportation and threatens public health.

Fires are a regular problem during the dry season in Indonesia, and the haze they generate has periodically drawn diplomatic complaints from neighboring countries in Southeast Asia.

AP Video by Muhammad Hatta

recentItems.title: Palestinians in central Gaza inspect damage caused by Israeli airstrikes
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Bureij, Central Gaza Strip – 25 August 2026 
1. Various of destruction after Israeli airstrike
2. People looking for their belongings in the rubble 
3. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Ali Naser, house destroyed by Israeli airstrike: 
”The order (the evacuation order) came, and we all went outside. No one knew where they would hit. We were shocked fifteen minutes after the call when the whole area was bombed. As you can see, about seven or eight houses were leveled. This was my house.”
4. Various of destruction 
5. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Ali Naser, house destroyed by Israeli airstrike:
”In a moment, in less than a second, all our dreams, memories, and all the hard work we'd put in over the years were destroyed by an Israeli missile. It didn't destroy the buildings; it destroyed our dreams and memories.”
6. Various of people recovering their belongings from rubble

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Deir Al-Balah, Central Gaza Strip – 25 August 2026 
7. Various of mosque partially destroyed after Israeli airstrike 
8. Sign at mosque's entrance, written in Arabic: "This mosque was built by Haj Muhammad Abu Salim from Deir al-Balah at his own expense, in the year 1370 AH, 1951 AD."
9. Various of destruction 
STORYLINE:
Palestinians on Tuesday inspected the destruction of a building in central Gaza that was hit by an Israeli airstrike the previous day, killing a 4-year-old child.

The strike hit the Bureij refugee camp after residents said they received an evacuation warning from the Israeli military. One family was unable to flee. The child’s mother and sister were wounded, according to Awda hospital.

AP footage showed collapsed concrete slabs, twisted metal and household belongings scattered across the area. A nearby mosque had a partially destroyed dome.

“This was my house,” said Ali Naser, whose home was flattened. He said at least seven houses were destroyed or damaged.

The strike was among several attacks in central and northern Gaza on Monday that killed at least four people, including the child. The attacks came after Israeli officials said the military would act forcefully against kite launches from Gaza.

Kites are among the few forms of entertainment available to Gaza children after more than two years of war.

Production by Wafaa Shurafa

recentItems.title: China’s Xi welcomes Jordan’s King Abdullah II in Beijing
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY:

AGENCY POOL
Beijing, China -  24 August 2026
1. Wide of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Jordanian King Abdullah II walking onto stage
2. Close of Xi and Abdullah
3. Various of Xi and Abdullah inspecting guards of honor
4. Xi and Abdullah smiling and waving at children   
5. Various of bilateral meetings 
6. Various of signing ceremony, Xi and Abdullah witnessing signing of documents 
7. Zoom out of Xi and Abdullah shaking hands 
STORYLINE:
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed Jordanian King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing on Monday, as the Jordanian monarch wrapped up his seven-day visit to China.

Xi held a welcome ceremony for Abdullah at the Great Hall of the People, followed by bilateral talks and a signing ceremony of cooperation documents.

During the meeting, Xi described the China-Jordan bilateral relationship as "a vivid example" of win-win cooperation between countries with different social systems and different sizes. 

China is ready to enhance strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and strengthen coordination and collaboration on multilateral platforms with Jordan so as to promote greater development of the strategic partnership between the two countries, Xi said. 

Abdullah expressed respect for China's model of development and economic growth, as well as its leadership on the international stage. 

He said the two sides had held in-depth discussions on deepening cooperation across a wide range of vital fields, including agriculture, technology, pharmaceuticals, tourism, education, and culture during his stay. 

On regional issues, Abdullah said Jordan and China are aligned on the need to achieve "comprehensive calm and stability" in the Middle East, so that the region's people can live in peace and prosperity. 

The two leaders witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents in areas such as diplomacy, trade and economy, industrial and supply chains, and the judiciary.

The king’s talks with Xi came after he visited Shanghai and Shenzhen, where he said he explored opportunities to deepen economic cooperation with China.

recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Seoul, South Korea - 25 August 2026
1. Various of South Korean Foreign Ministry regular briefing
2. SOUNDBITE (Korean) Park Doo-soon, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson:
"As stated in the joint fact sheet from the South Korea-U.S. summit last November, South Korea and the United States have consistently maintained their commitment to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula and to the goal of denuclearization. The two countries are pursuing North Korea policy in close coordination to achieve these objectives, and this was also discussed during the recent phone call between the South Korean and U.S. foreign ministers."
3. Wide of briefing
4. SOUNDBITE (Korean) Park Doo-soon, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson:
"Regarding the measures taken by both countries for peace on the Korean Peninsula through North Korea-U.S. dialogue, our position is that we hope North Korea will respond positively so that dialogue between North Korea and the U.S. can resume. As a peacemaker and a party to peace on the Korean Peninsula, our government is making active efforts, in close coordination with the United States toward the resumption of North Korea-U.S. dialogue and peace on the Korean Peninsula."
5. Wide pan of Park leaving
STORYLINE:
South Korean Foreign Ministry spokesperson said during Tuesday's regular briefing that both South Korea and the U.S. were committed to peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula and to the goal of denuclearization. 

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Park Doo-soon's statement came hours after it was reported that South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had agreed, during a phone conversation, to continue close communication to address the North Korean nuclear issue. 

"The two countries are pursuing North Korea policy in close coordination to achieve these objectives, and this was also discussed during the recent phone call between the Korean and U.S. foreign ministers," said Park.

During the briefing, a journalist also asked a question regarding U.S. President Donald Trump's posting of photos of himself and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. In response to the question, Park said South Korea is playing a role of a peacemaker and is "making active efforts, in close coordination with the United States, toward the resumption of North Korea-U.S. dialogue and peace on the Korean Peninsula."

Last week Trump announced on social media that he had ordered the military to substantially scale back the joint military exercise with South Korea, citing his good relationship with Kim. Trump also said that he would meet with Kim later this year.

recentItems.title: Indonesians brave choking smoke to pray for rain as country battles wildfires
recentItems.description:
(25 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Palembang, South Sumatra, Indonesia -  25 August 2026
1. Various of Muslim men and women sitting on carpets in an open field, waiting for prayers to begin
2. Various of  worshippers performing prayers
3. Men raising their hands in prayer, asking for rain to fall soon.
4. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Tony Kurniawan, worshipper and local resident:
++AUDIO QUALITY AS INCOMING++
“We are praying together and also asking for the support of all people in South Sumatra, so that rain will fall soon, the forest and land fires will end, and the air can return to normal.”
5. Ampera Bridge, an iconic landmark in South Sumatra, shrouded in thick haze
6. A boat carrying passengers traveling through the smoky haze
7. A fishermen’s settlement shrouded in thick haze
8. Rice fields blanketed by haze
9. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Umi Kalsum, local resident:
“The thick haze has disrupted traffic due to poor visibility. The dense smoke has also affected our throats and breathing, making it difficult to breathe.”
10. Various of firefighters battling flames spreading near a residential area
STORYLINE:
Authorities in Indonesia’s South Sumatra, the province with the highest number of wildfire hot spots, turned to spiritual measures on Tuesday as huge blazes in central and western regions scorched wide areas of forests and peatland, creating a choking haze that blanketed some cities in the world’s most populous Muslim-majority country.

The prayer gathering initiative comes as the province faces prolonged dry weather that has heightened the risk of forest and peatland fires.

The latest satellite data from the Environment Ministry showed South Sumatra recorded the highest number of hot spots nationwide with 1,429, followed by West Kalimantan with 1,226 and Central Kalimantan with 811. 

Forestry Ministry data indicated that nearly 940 square kilometers (363 square miles) were burned in July alone, including over 20 square kilometers (8 square miles) in South Sumatra province.

About 3,000 residents gathered in Palembang, the capital of South Sumatra province, to perform a special Islamic prayer for rain, known as “salat istisqa.” 

They prayed shoulder to shoulder in the courtyard of the governor’s office as thick smoke shrouded roads, buildings and public facilities, reducing visibility and forcing motorists to drive with their headlights on during the day.

South Sumatra Gov. Herman Deru said that everyone has done everything they can and worked closely with all relevant parties before the prayer. 

He added that as people of faith, they are praying to God to send rain so that life can return to normal.

He also said the public prayer would complement ongoing firefighting and drought-mitigation measures and serve as a moment for residents to unite in confronting the environmental challenges facing the province.

Emergency services have been battling fires driven by an intensifying El Nino pattern and a prolonged dry season, generating dense smoke that crossed into Malaysia and Brunei, according to the National Disaster Management Agency.

Indonesia is actively intensifying weather-modification operations to help firefighters combat wildfires by inducing rainfall through the dispersal of salt particles into suitable clouds, with 30 aircraft for cloud-seeding and water-bombing operations over Kalimantan, and another 22 helicopters covering Sumatra.



Fires are a regular problem during the dry season in Indonesia, and the haze they generate has periodically drawn diplomatic complaints from neighboring countries in Southeast Asia.
